published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'baryon density Omega_b h^2 = 0.0224 +- 0.0001 ... Assuming the base-LCDM cosmology, the inferred (model-dependent) late-Universe parameters are: Hubble constant H_0 = (67.4 +- 0.5) km s^-1 Mpc^-1 ... in significant, 3.6 sigma, tension with local measurements of the Hubble constant (which prefer a higher value).' Table 2 (TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing, 68%): Omega_b h^2 = 0.02237 +- 0.00015; H_0 = 67.36 +- 0.54; Age = 13.797 +- 0.023 Gyr; z_* = 1089.92 +- 0.25; (+BAO: 0.02242 +- 0.00014, 67.66 +- 0.42). Conclusions (p.71): 'The Planck base-LCDM cosmology requires a Hubble constant H_0 = (67.4 +- 0.5) ..., in substantial 4.4 sigma tension with the latest local determination by Riess et al. (2019).' 'We find good agreement between the predictions of BBN for the Planck base-LCDM parameters and element abundance observations.' The baryon-to-photon ratio eta is NOT printed in the 17 pages READ (checked by search); Planck's measured quantity is Omega_b h^2, and eta follows by the standard conversion with T_CMB = 2.7255 K and the mean mass per baryon (re-derived here: eta = (6.124 +- 0.041)e-10).
published_hypotheses: H1 base-LCDM: spatially flat, six parameters with flat priors, power-law adiabatic scalar spectrum, w = -1 (abstract; Table 1 caption).
H2 late-Universe parameters (H_0, Omega_m, age) are 'inferred (model-dependent)' under H1, not directly measured (abstract).
H3 one massive neutrino of 0.06 eV included in Omega_m; N_eff = 3.046 (Table 1 caption; abstract).
H4 helium fraction set by standard BBN, Y_P ~ 0.2454 (Table 2 caption); Omega_b h^2 is 'only weakly dependent on the cosmological model' (abstract).
H5 dataset/likelihood: TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing, Plik; 'A total systematic uncertainty of around 0.5 sigma may be more realistic' (Table 1 caption).
H6 T_CMB = 2.7255 K (Fixsen 2009) -- enters the eta conversion as T^-3.
H7 Planck's own recorded caveat: its H_0 is in 3.6 sigma (abstract) / 4.4 sigma (conclusions, vs Riess et al. 2019) tension with local measurements.
